subject: Post-demo: model fit & streaming UX follow-ups (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Dr. Lina Torres <lina.torres@acme-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Benson <tbenson@acme-health.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks for the demo — next steps

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo earlier — the team and I appreciated the walkthrough of Redwood’s streaming capabilities. A few quick notes from our side:

- We liked the idea of prefix caching for repeated prompts (could save a lot of tokens).
- Concerned about partial outputs in streaming mode — sometimes the assistant returns a sentence fragment that is confusing to clinicians.
- We need recommendations on model variants that balance latency and medical-quality coherence. Our infra team also asked about stop-sequence handling for multi-turn templates.

Next steps on our side: share a sample prompt set and a small dataset (de-identified) for a model-fit check. Could Redwood run a quick eval and share baseline recommendations? Also want an estimate of latency at our target 256-token responses.

Thanks,
Lina
Dr. Lina Torres
Clinical Informatics Lead, Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-18T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — next steps

Hi Lina — great to hear and thanks for the clear asks. Recapping action items so we’re aligned:

1) You share the de-identified prompt set and sample cases (Lina) — we’ll anchor evaluations to those prompts.
2) Redwood will run a model-fit eval (3 variants) and provide: recommended model, per-model BLEU/ROUGE-style metrics we use internally for instruction compliance, and qualitative failure modes.
3) We’ll pay attention to streaming UX issues: partial output coherence, stop-sequences, and token-level latency.

Initial model candidates we plan to test: Llama-2-Chat 13B (quantized 4-bit), Falcon-40B-instruct (fp16), and a Redwood-optimized 30B quantized variant we’ve seen good inference latency on. If you have preferred models, tell us and we’ll add them.

We’ll aim to deliver a short report and sample logs by EOD Tuesday (2026-06-23). If we see systemic streaming coherence problems tied to generation strategy, we’ll include recommended stop-sequence configs and a quick test harness you can run locally.

Attaching: prompt_set_acme_v2.csv (expected format) and a one-page eval plan.

Regards,
Marissa Cole

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Benson <tbenson@acme-health.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Dr. Lina Torres <lina.torres@acme-health.com>
Date: 2026-06-23T17:58:00-07:00
Subject: Acme evals: preliminary results + streaming log samples

Hi team — quick update from the run completed this afternoon. Summary (high level):

- Completed 1000 prompt runs across three variants on two instance classes. Attached: acme_model_eval_report_v1.pdf and streaming-playback-sample-logs.zip.
- Latency: avg token-level latency (p4d-like)
  - Llama-2-Chat-13B (4-bit): 22 ms/token median, 48 ms 95th
  - Redwood-30B-quant: 17 ms/token median, 40 ms 95th
  - Falcon-40B-instruct (fp16): 35 ms/token median, 80 ms 95th
- Coherence/partial-output: our partial-output detector flagged 7.8% of Llama-13B outputs, 4.1% for Redwood-30B-quant, and 10.2% for Falcon-40B. The flags correlate with mid-sentence stop indices and unusual punctuation patterns in the generated text.
- Stop sequences: we found that a conservative list ("\n\n", "\n-", "\n\u2022") plus enforcing final-token checks reduced incomplete-list truncations by ~60% in post-processing.

Recommendations:
1) For your latency target at 256 tokens and clinician-facing coherence, we recommend Redwood-30B-quant as the primary candidate (best tradeoff of latency + coherence).
2) Use explicit stop-sequence rules (we’ll provide a config) and a final-token heuristic to avoid mid-list truncation.
3) If you need highest factuality/regulatory consistency for long outputs, consider Falcon-40B-instruct as a fallback for batch jobs (accepts higher latency).

Next steps:
- Marissa/Jordan: share the short report with Lina + Tom (I attached), and we’ll annotate 30 sample transcripts for qualitative failures.
- Lina: if acceptable, we can run a longer 10k prompt pass on Redwood-30B-quant to further stabilize metrics (estimate 24-36 hours runtime).

Let me know if you want a quick walkthrough of the logs — I can schedule a 30-min session.

Thanks,
Dev

(attachments: acme_model_eval_report_v1.pdf, streaming-playback-sample-logs.zip)
